name: Projected Distinguishing Range / Combinatorial Eluder Dimension
details: The exact universal inequality $\mathrm R^p\ge\mathrm{Edim}$ is false. More strongly, no absolute constants C,D give $\mathrm{Edim}\le C\mathrm R^p+D$ on all finite binary classes: the triangular-code family has Edim equal to 2^n and projected distinguishing range at most 6n+5. The earlier four-concept class with values two and three remains a valid strict witness. This does not exclude all nonlinear bounds.
proof_source: Survey cor:eluder-range-affine-incomparable, using prop:triangular-code-range and the database-owned triangular-code endpoint values.
witness_verification: The database-owned values give Edim/Rp >= 2^n/(6n+5), which tends to infinity. All values are finite. The exact event/prefix probabilities and essential-projection characterization are replayed by sync/verify_triangular_range_separation.py.
